arrangement:
@length 64

0   section call            ; gong + low blues riff + 909 kick + elbow loop
0   in gong
0   in kick
0   in lead
0   in bass
# broods LOW on the blues scale. constant small variation, never a dead-repeat loop.

16  section reach-1         ; riff reaches up — fifth (g), b7 (bb), octave enter. VARY, don't layer.
16  set lead c2 ~ f2 ~  fs2 ~ g2 ~  bb2 ~ g2 ~  f2 eb2 ~ ~ c2 ~ g2 ~  c3 ~ bb2 ~  g2 ~ fs2 ~  f2 ~ eb2 ~ c2 ~ ~ ~  eb2 f2 fs2 g2  bb2 ~ ~ ~  g2 ~ f2 ~ c2 ~ f2 ~  fs2 ~ eb2 ~  c2 ~ g2 ~  c3 ~ ~ ~ /1

32  in gong

48  section reach-3         ; 606 hat enters soft; fifths + pitch-bend feel up top
48  in chh
48  gain chh 0.45 4
# loop: back to low brood. no drop. kept alive by VARYING the riff, not adding drama.
# REMINDER: humanize organ timing (no-quantize) or the hypnotism is only half-present.

meta.title: Plastic Dreams (essence portrait, blues + elbow)
meta.essence: ONE deep organ riff played on the C BLUES SCALE (C Eb F F# G Bb), hand-played and DELIBERATELY UNQUANTIZED (slightly off-grid), over layered classic drum machines and an accidental looping 'elbow' bass texture. Hypnotic via constant riff VARIATION, not a single repeated loop. Form: broods low (oct 2) then reaches up using fifths + the octave.
meta.inspiration: Jaydee — 'Plastic Dreams' (1992). COPYRIGHTED work; this is an inspired-by homage using the generic four-on-floor idiom + an ORIGINAL circling riff evoking the deep-organ character, NOT a transcription.
meta.sourceOfTruth: Pitches/register from a user Ableton screenshot (C2/D#2/F2/F#2, 129 BPM, 16-bar). Production facts from a deconstruction video: TX81Z FM organ (lpf+delay+reverb); 909 kick+clap, 606 hats, 808 cymbal/maracas; hip-hop breaks (EQ'd/HPF'd); blues-scale riffs; NO quantization (off-grid by intent); riffs constantly varied; accidental 'elbow' low-key loop (belly bit, ~JD-800); fifths + pitch-bend(4) later.
meta.scale: C blues (C, Eb, F, F#, G, Bb) — NOT plain C minor. The F#(#4/b5) is the blues hook.
meta.pitchSet: C blues: c2 eb2 f2 fs2 g2 bb2 (+ reach c3 eb3 f3 fs3). Riff vocabulary = this scale.
meta.designPrinciple: ESSENCE-FIRST, NOT TEMPLATE. RESTRAINT IS THE RULE. Only kick + the single organ riff + the elbow loop + a rare gong. NO chord stabs, NO arp, NO busy hats, NO section-swap drama. Evolution happens INSIDE the riff via slow mutation, not by adding tracks.

originalInstruments.organ: Renamed to 'lead' — the engine has no organ voice. Intended timbre: Yamaha TX81Z FM (4-op), low-pass filtered, delay + reverb. FM not subtractive — model with a 2-op FM voice if possible; the studio's supersaw is wrong.
originalInstruments.elbow: Renamed to 'bass' — its sawtooth + resonant LPF in the low register approximates the JD-800-ish 'belly body + rhythmic click' character of the source's accidental loop. JayDee knocked the lowest synth key with his elbow reaching for a drink, liked it, looped it for the whole track.
originalInstruments.gong: Track kept by name; silent until a gong voice exists. 'in gong' cues are no-ops for now.
originalInstruments.kick_clap_hats: Source uses 909 kick, 909 clap, 606 hats, 808 cymbal/maracas. The engine's generic 'kick' / 'chh' / 'clap' voices stand in; voice-design task, flagged.

meta.NO_QUANTIZE_REQUIREMENT: CRITICAL: the source riff must NOT sit perfectly on the grid. JayDee refused to quantize and that off-grid humanity is THE defining feature (labels called it 'wrong'; it is why the track endures). The studio's rigid 16th grid quantizes everything = it CANNOT reproduce the essence as-is. Needs a per-note timing-jitter / swing-humanize feature (offset each onset by a few ms, randomized). Until then this preset is structurally faithful but rhythmically TOO CLEAN. This is the #1 engine requirement for this piece.

essenceNotes.bluesScaleCorrection: The four screenshot notes C/Eb/F/F# are the first four degrees of the C BLUES scale, not 'C minor with a chance tritone'. The riff vocabulary IS the blues scale; later sections add the 5th (G), b7 (Bb), and the octave for the soaring runs. Generative variation = move within C blues, not C minor.
essenceNotes.theElbow: A genuine accident: JayDee knocked the lowest synth key with his elbow reaching for a drink, liked the rhythmic low 'belly' texture, and looped it for the whole track. It is a co-equal spine with the drums and organ. Modeled here as a low irregular pulse on the bass voice.
essenceNotes.humanity: The no-quantize, hand-played, off-grid timing is the track's most defining trait. A perfectly gridded rendition is — by the creator's own logic — a failure. See NO_QUANTIZE_REQUIREMENT.
essenceNotes.cymaticsCoupling: A near-static spectrum dominated by one low-mid riff + a low rhythmic pulse = a steady, slowly-breathing field that shifts subtly as the riff varies. The visual hypnotism mirrors the musical hypnotism — exactly because nothing busy is competing.

caveats.copyright: Original is copyrighted; this reproduces only the generic four-on-floor idiom + an ORIGINAL riff evoking the character. Homage, not cover.
caveats.quantization: The studio quantizes to a 16th grid; the source's essence is the REFUSAL to quantize. This preset is rhythmically too clean until a humanize/timing-jitter feature exists. Engine requirement #1 for this piece.
caveats.tempoTrick: The fast organ runs may have been recorded at ~60 BPM and sped up. The grid can approximate density but not that performance nuance.
caveats.restraintIsFragile: Resist the urge to 'improve' this by adding parts. If it starts sounding busy, the essence is lost. Any addition must be tiny and late.

lessonsForSkill: Production research can OVERTURN a transcription's interpretation: the same four notes are 'C minor + odd note' or 'C blues scale' depending on context — and the latter gives the correct generative vocabulary. Always seek the scale/intent, not just the pitches.

Some essences are PERFORMANCE, not notes: no-quantize humanity, accidental textures (the elbow), tempo tricks. Capture them as explicit engine requirements + documented intent, never silently quantize them away.
When a transcription source exists (screenshot/MIDI/score), READ IT — do not harmonize from theory. Register and the 'wrong' note are often the essence.
Accidental textures count as essence. The elbow loop is not garnish — it is one of three co-equal spines (kick / organ / elbow). Preserve it as a first-class track, not as a nice-to-have.
Signature timbre is a separate task: TX81Z FM organ, JD-800 elbow body, TR-909/606/808 drums. Pattern + scale captured here; voice-design flagged.
